questions.q: What is AI Builder, in relation to Power Automate?
options: A separate product requiring its own sign-up and license portal
A Power Platform feature that exposes AI models as actions you can use inside flows and apps
A replacement for the flow designer
A third-party connector maintained outside Microsoft
questions.explain: AI Builder lives inside the same Power Platform environment as Power Automate and Power Apps, exposing AI models as actions rather than requiring a separate product.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a prebuilt model and a custom model in AI Builder?
options: Prebuilt models cost more
Custom models can only be used in Power Apps, never in Power Automate
A prebuilt model is already trained by Microsoft and ready to use; a custom model you train yourself on your own sample data
There is no real difference
questions.explain: Prebuilt models arrive trained on general data. Custom models require you to supply your own sample data, such as Castlebridge Logistics' own delivery-confirmation layout, and run them through training.

questions.q: Where do you go inside Power Automate to explore and try AI Builder models?
options: The Approvals menu
AI hub
The Data tab
Solutions
questions.explain: AI hub, in Power Automate's left navigation, is the catalog where every AI Builder model category — prebuilt and custom — is explored, tried, and built.

questions.q: Which three AI Builder model categories does this chapter focus on?
options: Document processing, classification, and prompts
Forecasting, anomaly detection, and recommendation
Robotic process automation, chatbots, and data loss prevention
Translation, transcription, and speech synthesis only
questions.explain: Document processing (Lesson 8), classification (Lesson 9), and prompts (Lessons 10-12) are the three categories this chapter covers.

questions.q: How does an AI Builder action behave once it's added to a flow, compared to other actions you learned in Chapter 1?
options: It requires a completely different designer outside Power Automate
It can't take inputs from earlier steps in the flow
It slots in the same way any action does — taking inputs like a file or dynamic content, and returning outputs you reference downstream
It can only be the very first step in a flow
questions.explain: An AI Builder action is still just an action: it accepts inputs the same way an HTTP action or condition would, and its outputs (fields, scores, generated text) become dynamic content for later steps.
